That is dedup-before-minting applied to Knox's own proposal, and it is the difference between a new governance object and an inherited discipline.\n\n---\n\n## §1 — OUTPUT 1 · The care-financing operating-profile map\n\n### §1.1 What the profile is — corrected at R1\n**The Mixed Financing Operating Profile is a governed cross-plane composition *and conformance* contract. The versioned derived assessment is one artifact produced under it, not the whole of it.**\n\nR0 equated the profile with its assessment record, which forced the §11 conclusion that three anti-shadow criteria were undemonstrable. That conclusion was an artifact of the boundary, not of the architecture.\n\n**It owns conformance. It owns no source truth, and it holds no commit authority.** Conformance operates at two altitudes and they must not be merged: **build-time** (gates a build must pass, modelled on C4.6 `C1`–`C16`) and **run-time** (invariants plus an audit surface — the Law 2 read-set boundary is the only genuinely run-time member, §6.3).\n\n**Four strata, named profile-locally.** `MFP-` is deliberately not `P-`: the canonical **P0–P6** plane taxonomy is owned by the Surface Map header and these are not architecture planes.\n\n| Stratum | Contents | Owner | Write posture |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **`MFP-1` source** | payer coverage/benefit/formulary positions · determinations · authorizations · guarantees · sponsorships · loan approvals · pharmacy availability and offers · patient consent/preference/affordability · D6 orders, entitlements, money-state, `financing_arrangement` · Care/CM clinical assertions | **native owners and external principals**, unchanged | each owner writes its own |\n| **`MFP-2` exchange** | crossing, identity, represented principal + capacity, delegated authority, consent/grant, returned-state classification (`evidence` · `observation` · `proposed-meaning` · `externally_committed_truth`) | **GCE** (ratified, `tier0_mandatory`, bidirectional, insurance an enumerated subfamily) | classifies; commits nothing by arrival |\n| **`MFP-3` assessment** | the versioned mixed-financing assessment: rule identity + version, pinned inputs, dependency map, validity posture, dependency-scoped invalidation, recomputation, audience policy, issuance, lineage, proof | a **hard projection** under T0-15 — durable and composed, **never a second source of truth**; instance owner deferred to C5 (§2) | writes only its own derived record; supersedes, never mutates |\n| **`MFP-4` operating** | attention, deadline, queue, work ownership, operative posture while unresolved, escalation, next-action-and-clock, redress coordination | **CNS** orchestration; obligations from a stance via **OFC**; conditional **Accountability** above the §5.5 duty threshold | writes work state; **work state is never care state** |\n\n### §1.2 The direction law — three parts, replacing R0's single wrong sentence\nR0 said *\"no arrow returns.\"* That is false and this result contradicted it two sections later by relying on authorized outbound commands. Appeals, prior-authorization submissions, evidence responses, clinical recommits, financing applications and redress all require action to travel outward and consequence to return. Knox's replacement — *no direct reverse mutation* — is correct but under-determined: it does not say what stops \"the profile originates work\" from becoming \"the profile acts.\"\n\n**The law is three-part, and all three are load-bearing:**\n\n1. **No reverse mutation.** Nothing at `MFP-3` or `MFP-4` writes into `MFP-1`. Ever.\n2. **The profile may compose a command; it may never authorize one.** A proposal leaving `MFP-4` carries **no authority of its own**. Authority is supplied by a principal through RBAC/delegated capability at `MFP-2`, and the **commit is always the owning domain's**. This is the clause that prevents composition from manufacturing authority, and it is C4.6's `C5` (authority-bound action) and `C7` (command ≠ evidence ≠ commit) applied to financing.\n3. **Evidence returns; it does not adopt.** A returning result re-enters at `MFP-2` **with its classification intact** and invalidates or recomputes `MFP-3`. Returning does not make it true, and it never reaches `adoption_authority` for a care fact.\n\n**Knox's contribution and the correction to it, stated plainly:** Knox restored the return path, which R0 wrongly closed. Clause 2 is the addition — without it, \"the profile may originate work and candidate actions\" is one careless build away from the shadow authority Axis 1 exists to prevent.\n\n### §1.3 What the map still does not contain\nNo case object, episode object, negotiation object, coverage object, position store, fourth authoritative graph, or universal Insurance state machine. **The episode remains a projection over distributed artifacts and commits** (C4.6 §4, inherited).\n\n---\n\n## §2 — OUTPUT 2 · Derived assessment ownership (A-Q12)\n\n### §2.1 The pattern anchor, correctly scoped\n`public.eligibility_decisions` (`20260504120000_intake_foundation_v1.sql` L250–270) ships a versioned-derived-record shape: `rule_id` + `rule_version` · `input_refs` · `inputs_hash` · `input_snapshot` · `decided_at` · typed `decided_by` · `decided_by_user_id` · `supersedes_decision_id` · `interaction_context`.\n\n**R0 cited this as evidence for D6 ownership. It is not, and Knox is right.** The table is in the **Intake foundation** migration. It proves a **reusable record pattern**; it establishes no owner.\n\n| Safe to inherit | Must NOT be inherited |\n|---|---|\n| rule/version pin · source/input pin · content hash · computation identity · assessment timestamp · supersession chain · interaction context | `result in ('eligible','review_required','blocked')` — **`blocked` is not a mixed-financing status** · `provider_override` as a universal assessment authority · pathway-eligibility semantics · **Intake or D6 ownership inferred from the existence of a similar table** |\n\n### §2.2 The ownership decomposition — and the contract/instance split Knox blurred\n**A-Q12 closes at the lifecycle-decomposition level only. Runtime placement is C5.**\n\n| Responsibility | Owner |\n|---|---|\n| source positions | native domains and external principals |\n| composition rule definitions + versions | **Settings/Catalog** |\n| commercial allocation, patient responsibility, financing arithmetic | **D6** |\n| admissible set and selection output | **Sourcing** (distinct lifecycle, C4.6 §9) |\n| care-set effect, recommit rationale, reliance | **Care / REV-184 / CNS** |\n| work, queues, clocks, escalation | **CNS** |\n| issued artifact custody and delivery | **D7 + Messaging** |\n| the communicative commitment itself | **still open — H-N3/G7** |\n| **assessment conformance requirements** — identity, dependency map, validity posture, dependency-scoped invalidation, replay semantics | **the profile *contract*** |\n| **the assessment *instance*** — who computes it, where it lives, who operates it | **deferred to C5** |\n\n**O-8, correcting Knox.** Knox assigns \"snapshot identity, dependency map, validity posture, replay/invalidation semantics\" to the profile while also saying the profile \"owns conformance, not truth.\" Both can be true only if **contract and instance are separated**: the contract owns the *requirements*, the instance owns the *record*. Collapsing them re-creates the coordinator by a quieter route. A-Q12 therefore closes as *resolved-at-decomposition*, and **not** as \"the profile owns the assessment.\"\n\n**Invalidation is dependency-scoped, not a global boolean** (Knox, accepted and adopted): a payer policy expiry invalidates the coverage-dependent claims without pretending a recorded loan repayment, a patient preference or a prior clinical recommendation disappeared.\n\n### §2.3 O-6 — a naming hazard worth recording before it costs someone a week\n`eligibility_decisions` is **pathway** eligibility — is a patient eligible for a care pathway. It is **not** payer eligibility. The two are unrelated, and the table is the first hit for any future insurance work that searches the estate for \"eligibility.\" Combined with `payer_eligibility_documents.eligibility_status` — *\"one enum doing four jobs\"* — the word `eligibility` now means at least three different things across the committed estate. **Recorded as a hazard, routed to `FWREG-020`'s neighbourhood; no rename proposed and none authorized here.**\n\n---\n\n## §3 — OUTPUT 3 · Layered coverage scoping — the four scopes and how they compose\n\n| # | Scope | Source-authoritative at | OMNI holds | Composition rule |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **1** | **Coverage relationship identity** | **external payer or program** | an attributed projection under GCE | supplies the *subject*; every other layer references it and **none may redefine it** |\n| **2** | **Artifact + projection custody** | **operator/tenant**, purpose- and visibility-controlled (D7 + Federation grants) | canonical for the **artifact**, never the **coverage fact** | may *evidence* layer 1; **may never constitute it** — the exact fusion defect in `payer_eligibility_documents` |\n| **3** | **Operator/provider/episode applicability** | **operator-scoped**: D6 + Federation + Settings | canonical for the operator's own position | **layer-3 truth is not portable** — deployment-relative by construction, never published as a property of the person |\n| **4** | **Person-portable longitudinal view** | **nobody — noncanonical by definition** | a permissioned, source-preserving **hard projection** (T0-15) | composes 1+2+3 read-only, per-audience, with `as_of`; **acquires no write path and no gate role** |\n\n**The composition law:** *identity is referenced, custody is evidenced, applicability is operator-relative, portability is projected — and no layer may be promoted into the layer above it.*\n\n**Two detectable failure modes.** **Upward promotion** — a layer-2 artifact treated as layer-1 identity; already committed in `payer_eligibility_documents`, contained by `FWREG-020` clause 2, not fixed. **Sideways leakage** — a layer-3 operator applicability fact rendered in a layer-4 portable view as a property of the person's coverage; **no existing control blocks this**, and §15's patient-experience invariant is the first place it becomes visible.\n\n---\n\n## §4 — OUTPUT 4 · Commitment taxonomy (A-Q1a / A-Q1b), plus constitution mode\n\n**A-Q1a — accepted custody.** Named **ABSENT** by C4.3 §4; candidates Federation + RBAC. Existing machinery: the ten-state external-custody ladder and **`O10 ACK ≠ accepted-custody`** (mutation-tested `M04`, caught).\n\n**A-Q1b — substantive commitment**, seven kinds distinguished by obligor, expiry, revocation, breach and correction law:\n\n| Kind | Obligor | Expiry | Revocation | Breach | Correction law |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| authorization | payer | dated/service-scoped | prospective; retroactive-invalidity is C4.3 **S20-B** | funding denied; **care unaffected** (Law 1) | effective-time reassignment |\n| guarantee of payment | payer/sponsor/operator | until performance or lapse | conditional | financial | additive adjustment |\n| sponsorship | sponsor | program period | program terms | financial + **sponsor ≠ payer boundary (unowned, G6)** | program-native |\n| loan approval | lender | offer window | credit-policy | **obligor substitution**; refund destination becomes legal (`B-Q1`) | `financing_arrangement`-native |\n| network participation / rate terms | payer ↔ operator, **bilateral** | term | notice | contractual | **no carrier — contested state unrepresentable** |\n| contractual obligation (other) | any | instrument-specific | instrument-specific | contractual | instrument-specific |\n| coverage determination | payer | as-of dated | payer supersession only | none — a *determination*, not an undertaking | **OMNI never edits it** |\n\n**Constitution mode — a second axis, adopted from Knox and credited.** *How was the obligation constituted?* — `unilateral_determination` · `unilateral_undertaking` · `bilateral_agreement` · `statutory_entitlement_or_duty` · `delegated_authorization` · `externally_imposed_directive` · `accepted_transfer_or_custody`. A powerful principal's command does not erase an independent professional or safety duty.*\n\n**Generic authority physics above Insurance.** Routes to A-Q16 / C3.6C + RBAC + CNS + Care — **not** into Insurance, and not into a new domain.\n\n### §12.2 O-3 — conjunctive admission is the general form, and it is the physics of care\nThe aviation import and the nuclear-command intuition are **the same mechanism seen from two sides**, and naming it once is better than importing it twice.\n\n> **Conjunctive admission.** An execution proceeds only when **every** non-fungible predicate holds. **Any** predicate-holder may withhold. Withholding is not a contest of authority — it is the absence of a condition. No holder thereby acquires any other holder's authority.\n\n14 CFR 121.663 and 121.533(c)(3) are one instance: **conjunctive commit** (both must believe) with a **disjunctive veto** (either opinion cancels). Care is the same shape with more predicates:\n\n| Predicate | Holder | Withholding means |\n|---|---|---|\n| clinical intent and indication | treating clinician | not clinically indicated |\n| consent | patient | refused |\n| professional acceptance within scope | pharmacist / executing professional | not accepted for execution |\n| funding posture | payer / funder | not funded (**never** \"not indicated\") |\n| availability and custody | supply owner / pharmacy | not available |\n| money state | D6 | not settled |\n\n**This is why no single principal — EHR, payer portal, pharmacy system, lender or clearinghouse — can legitimately own the interaction end to end: each holds one predicate.** It is also the precise reason Axis 2 exists: *something must compose the predicates without owning any of them.*\n\n**The transfer limit, stated with the mechanism so it cannot be separated from it:** conjunctive admission must **never** be read as giving a payer a co-equal vote on a clinical act. The payer's predicate is *funding*, and its withholding produces *not funded* — which changes feasibility (Law 3) and never changes indication (Law 1). **A dual-concurrence model that let a payer's predicate speak to clinical merit would invert Law 2 while appearing to formalize it, and that is the most dangerous available misreading of the aviation import.**\n\n### §12.3 Multi-axis typing, the three branches, and the two anti-shadow failures\n**Typing axes:** GCE principal + represented capacity (**ratified, primary**) · C4.6 plane (**accepted L2, primary**) · speech-act kind (**OPEN**, typed at §4) · REV-184 stance + authority gate · `seam_kind` cross-loop effect (**candidate; admissible only where reuse is proven — used nowhere here, because no trace required it. Weak evidence against its necessity, not proof against its validity**).\n\n**Prohibitions obeyed:** nothing typed by `seam_kind`; a clinician recommit is **not** an accepted `custody_handoff` (submission ≠ acceptance; `O10 ACK ≠ accepted-custody`); a pharmacy substituting inside an already-authorized envelope is a **professional/execution commit**, not a `control_request`.\n\n**The three branches:** **(a)** clerical/operational reroute — operationally equivalent, executing principal within its envelope, **no reopen** · **(b)** permitted change inside an existing substitution/authority envelope, **authority basis recorded**, no reopen · **(c)** clinical reinterpretation — **authorized clinical recommit**, `reopen_care`. Discriminator inherited from C4.6 L205; **`C12` is the runnable gate and it fails when \"normalization and clinical change are indistinguishable\" or \"a permitted substitution lacks its authority basis.\"**\n\n**Failure 1 — the profile becomes the authoritative owner of the resolution.** Not triggered: `MFP-3` holds derived assessments, `MFP-4` holds work state, the resolution is REV-184/CNS-owned, commits are owning-domain.\n\n**Failure 2 — A-Q15, a fourth *authoritative* graph.** Not triggered; this gate names no new graph. Grades and currency per source are pinned at §0.3.\n\n### §14.1 Palantir — O-5, correcting both R0 and Knox\n**Consult `comparator_analogy_registry.md` first (Knox, right).** The registry already carries a substantial Palantir posture: **TAKE** executable objects/relationships/actions/dynamic-security; **REJECT** proprietary ontology gravity, semantic lock-in, and the claim that controlling the representation equals owning the domain. **The core negative transfer is not a new discovery**, and R0 should have cited the row rather than re-deriving it. What is new is the *application to A-Q15*.\n\n**Verified mechanism, from primary docs.** The Ontology is *\"an operational layer\"* over integrated assets, with **semantic elements** (object/property/link types) and **kinetic elements** (action types, functions, dynamic security). **Action types are governed transactions** editing objects, properties and links in one shot including side effects; the **Actions service** enforces *\"complex permissions and conditions\"* and produces *\"a historical action log for analysis of user decisions.\"* The **Object Data Funnel** *\"reads data from Foundry datasources **and user edits (from Actions)** and indexes these data into object databases.\"*\n\n**The peering question, verified — and this is where R0 and Knox are both wrong in opposite directions.**\n\n- **R0's \"inside one enrollment\" is stale and is withdrawn.** **Peer Manager** establishes connections that \"share data between distinct spaces across **two Foundry enrollments**,\" where the connection controls \"the types of data that may peer, **the direction** the data will peer, and the set of classification and other markings that can peer.\" Peerable: \"Foundry objects, object sets configured in Object Explorer, and Gotham files.\"\n- **Knox's \"Palantir now federates typed operational ontologies including mapped objects/links\" over-reads.** Palantir's own developer community answers the cross-ontology link question directly: **\"At the moment, no there is no way to do this. But we are tracking this as a feature request,\"** with a documented workaround of **duplicating the object into each ontology** and faking the link by foreign-key filtering. Peer Manager itself notes other resources (e.g. Workshop applications) do not yet peer.\n\n> **The corrected finding, and the wording proposed for the registry row:**\n> **Palantir peers *data* across enrollments; it does not peer the *ontology*.** Object data and object sets cross under a directional, marking-controlled connection, while the **semantic layer — link types, the relational structure that makes an ontology an ontology — does not cross**, and the documented workaround is duplication. Decisively, **peering presupposes platform symmetry and mutual configuration: both sides run Foundry and jointly agree the connection.**\n> **The OMNI non-transfer is therefore neither \"Palantir cannot cross organizational boundaries\" (stale) nor \"Palantir federates ontologies, so the moat is gone\" (unsupported).** It is that **peering solves federation between co-platformed, consenting enrollments, and OMNI's problem is asymmetric, non-consenting, non-co-platformed principals** — a payer, a pharmacy, a lender and a patient will not be co-enrolled in one vendor's platform by mutual configuration. **OMNI's differentiation is not that Palantir cannot federate; it is that OMNI supplies the healthcare-specific constitution — nonfungible authority, consent and refusal, clinical adoption, source sovereignty, care-versus-financing separation, decision-time rationale, correction-driven reopening, longitudinal care consequence — that must remain true whichever substrate realizes part of the implementation.**\n\n**A-Q15 pressure result:** the answer at §12.3 is unchanged and its justification is stronger. Three coexisting graphs is not an OMNI eccentricity to be tidied into one; it is the consequence of cross-sovereign truth. The single-graph alternative has a named owner, a real mechanism, and now a precisely-bounded reach. **Multiplicity is the price of sovereignty — and, per Knox, kill condition 3's differentiator must be restated on the corrected basis, which §10 does.**\n\n**Adjacent technology mechanisms — carried at inherited maturity, explicitly not re-derived, and marked incomplete where they are.** **AWS saga/compensation:** the carrier's R5 correction stands — a *proposal* discloses expected tradeoffs and reversibility; a *committed consequential transition* declares its rollback/mitigation/reopen path where one exists and **names the residual irreversible consequence where one does not**; per F6 no compensating action may claim to restore lost care state. Corrections are **owner-native new commits plus assessment invalidation/replay, not one distributed rollback** (Knox, adopted). **Anthropic/OpenAI-class platforms:** *approval enforced in the tool, not the prompt* — capability-specific authorization **outside** the model layer, which is direct support for §6.3's read-set boundary being structural rather than instructional. **Tesla:** degraded sensing makes automation *unavailable* rather than letting the system pretend inputs are good — maps cleanly onto stale/unknown payer, benefit or availability evidence: **degrade the profile's automation and confidence, never the source truth** (Knox, adopted; a genuinely useful addition). **Epic:** configuration-as-truth, per-customer instances and customer-specific implementation — which is why kill condition 3 is about cross-counterparty coherence, not features. **These four are consulted at inherited/secondary depth, not independently re-verified this pass, and are marked incomplete accordingly.**\n\n### §14.2 Military / joint C2 — pinned, and downgraded for currency\n**Source pinned: JP 1, *Doctrine for the Armed Forces of the United States*, Incorporating Change 1, 12 July 2017**, obtained from a third-party mirror, **not** `jcs.mil`.\n\n**Currency, stated because Knox was right to demand it: this edition is SUPERSEDED.** JP 1 was restructured into **JP 1 Volume 1, *Joint Warfighting* (27 Aug 2023)** and **JP 1 Volume 2, *The Joint Force* (2020)** — and Vol 2 is the volume that now carries the organization and **command-and-control mechanisms** material, i.e. exactly the passages quoted below. **Current JPs are CAC-restricted on `jcs.mil` and were not obtained;** terminology is canonically maintained in the DoD Dictionary, also not obtained. **These quotes are therefore evidence-grade with a named currency caveat and MUST NOT become acceptance-grade until re-verified against JP 1 Vol 2.** The mechanisms are long-standing and structural, which is why the *transfer* survives the caveat; the *citations* do not.\n\n| Mechanism (verified in the 2017 edition) | Transfer |\n|---|---|\n| *\"Authority is never absolute; the extent of authority is specified by the establishing authority, directives, and law.\"* | **TAKE — the doctrine-level statement of scoped, instrument-granted authority.** Direct A-Q16 support |\n| *\"TACON does not provide organizational authority or authoritative direction for administrative and logistic support.\"* | **TAKE — the strongest single A-Q16 finding.** A mature discipline enumerates what an authority does **not** reach. A payer's funding authority should be specified the same way |\n| **ADCON vs OPCON** — two orthogonal authority channels over the same unit | **TAKE.** Administrative/financial and operational/clinical authority over the same act are **parallel, not ranked** — what a single `authority_rank` ladder cannot express |\n| **Support relationship + establishing directive** — specifies *\"the purpose… the effect desired, the scope of action to be taken, and any shifts in the support relationship\"* | **TAKE the shape.** But per Knox: this is constituted by an **establishing authority**, so it is **not** evidence of a bilateral carrier. It supports the **constitution-mode axis** at §4 instead |\n| *\"When a supporting commander cannot fulfill the needs of the supported commander, the establishing authority will be notified by either the supported commander or a supporting commander. The establishing authority is responsible for determining a solution.\"* | **TAKE the structure, REJECT the presupposition.** Non-fulfilment is a **first-class declarable state**, **either party may escalate**, and a **named third authority** resolves. This is the first located mechanism for *\"payer will not fund / pharmacy cannot supply\"* that treats the supporting party as neither obedient nor silent — **but healthcare has no establishing authority**, which is why kill condition 6 survives |\n| **Coordinating authority** — *\"a consultation relationship between commanders, **not an authority by which C2 may be exercised**… does not have the authority to resolve disputes\"* | **TAKE — the closest external name for what the operating profile is.** Independent confirmation that \"coordinates, cannot decide\" is a real operating category with bounded use, not a euphemism for a weak domain |\n| **Multinational OPCON reservations** — an MNFC *\"cannot change the mission… nor separate units, divide their supplies, administer discipline\"*; US commanders *\"maintain the capability to report to higher US military authorities in addition to MNFCs\"* | **TAKE.** Granting control **enumerates non-transferable reservations** and **preserves an independent reporting path** — a payer may commit funding without acquiring clinical recommit authority, and the patient/clinician retains an escalation channel the funding relationship cannot close |\n| **Unity of effort vs unity of command** — other departments' operations *\"are not under command of the Armed Forces\"*; multinational unity of command *\"may not be politically feasible\"* | **TAKE the concept and its cost.** Doctrine does not pretend coordination without a commander equals command; it names it differently and accepts weaker guarantees. **OMNI should do the same rather than implying the profile delivers command-grade coherence** |\n\n**Transfer limits, tested rather than asserted.** **(i) No universal commander — HOLDS, more sharply than the carrier claimed:** doctrine's own no-common-commander branch is unity of effort + coordinating authority, which is a better fit than the command hierarchy. **(ii) Logistics authority is independent — HOLDS and is evidence-backed:** COCOM includes *\"authoritative direction over all aspects of military operations, joint training, and **logistics**,\"* so logistics **is** subordinate in military doctrine, and that is exactly what must not transfer. **(iii) Mission economics do not transfer — HOLDS, untested and untestable here.**\n\n### §14.3 Civil aviation — the joint-release question answered, the tie-break claim narrowed\n**Verified verbatim** (14 CFR part 121, pinned): **§121.533(b)** *\"The pilot in command and the aircraft dispatcher are **jointly responsible** for the preflight planning, delay, and dispatch release.\"* **§121.663** *\"…shall sign the release **only if they both believe** that the flight can be made with safety.\"* **§121.533(c)(3)** dispatcher cancels or redispatches *\"if, in **his opinion or the opinion of the pilot in command**,\"* the flight cannot operate safely. **§121.533(d)–(e)** in flight the PIC has *\"full control and authority… without limitation.\"* **§121.627(a)** no continuation if either judges it unsafe, *\"unless, in the opinion of the pilot in command, there is no safer procedure. In that event, continuation… is an **emergency situation** as set forth in §121.557.\"* **§121.557(b)** the dispatcher *\"shall advise… shall **ascertain the decision** of the pilot in command, and shall **have the decision recorded**,\"* and if it cannot communicate, *\"shall declare an emergency and take any action that he considers necessary.\"* **§121.557(c)** a written report within **10 days**. **§121.601** an affirmative, continuing **duty to inform**, separate from decision authority.\n\n**Six mechanisms.** **(1) Conjunctive commit, disjunctive veto** — generalized at §12.2 as **conjunctive admission**. **(2) Phase-dependent authority** — joint before departure, PIC dominant in flight; authority is scoped by phase, not held statically. **(3) Exceptional-regime transition — NARROWED at R1 (R1-07, Knox correct).** R0's framing, *\"disagreement resolves by regime change, not override,\"* is **too broad**: §§121.627/121.557 govern **unsafe continuation and emergencies**, not any disagreement, and emergency authority is bounded to situations *requiring immediate decision and action* and carries reporting duties. **The correct import is narrow: phase-bounded conjunctive admission over separate non-fungible commits, with explicit *exceptional-regime* transitions — not a universal tie-break and not one shared authority.** **(4) Degraded-communication fallback with a named unilateral actor** — degraded mode names *who* may act alone, in advance; OMNI's *\"who acts when the payer does not respond?\"* currently resolves only to `T-13`'s declared consequence, which names a consequence but not an actor. **(5) Deviation is permitted but never silent** — the exception path produces a durable accountability artifact by construction; strong external validation of *non-action-as-commit* and *silence is not closure*. **(6) Duty to inform ≠ share of the decision** — a clean analogue for the payer's obligation to state policy, deadlines and evidence requirements without acquiring clinical authority.\n\n**Transfer limits.** **REJECT the shared employer** — PIC and dispatcher work for one certificate holder under one operations specification, and the joint responsibility is created by a **regulator**; OMNI's principals share neither. The mechanism transfers; **the institutional container that makes it enforceable does not.** **REJECT the symmetric safety objective** — both aviation parties are bound to *\"can this flight be made safely\"*; a payer is not bound to the patient's clinical objective (§12.2's named misreading). **REJECT the single operational tempo** — aviation's joint release is minutes-to-hours; payer/pharmacy/patient resolution runs for days to months, asynchronously, with parties changing. **The concurrence mechanism must survive A-Q17's partial order before it can be imported, and A-Q17 is unresolved.**\n\n### §14.4 `M-202` composite incumbent — steelmanned element by element at R1\nR0 asserted a conclusion. ## Assistant

Knox's review was strong and largely right. Eleven of its thirteen patches survived verification and are in. Two I corrected back. And the single best result in this round came from doing exactly what Knox told me to do — open C4.6 instead of citing it unread.

**The headline: Law 2's enforcement mechanism was never missing. It was already built, and all three of us walked past it.**

R0 said the structural enforcement of the economic-influence firewall was *owed*. Knox independently proposed a test for it as new work — mutate operator margin, lender revenue, manufacturer economics while holding clinical evidence fixed, and require the clinically ranked option set to stay invariant. When I opened C4.6 §7 properly I found gate **`C6`**, accepted L2 build doctrine, landed on `main` since July:

> **C6 | Neutrality / incentive firewall | margin-only counterfactual test | FAILS if changing operator margin changes clinical authorization, or hides incentive lineage in selection.**

The pharmacy arc built the runnable proof shape for this law and nobody in the Insurance arc knew. That is the estate's signature failure — *physics written down in several places with nobody in the room at once* — reproduced by two reviewers of a gate whose own §16 names that exact failure mode. The consequence is large and cheap: Law 2 moves from *invent enforcement* to *extend an existing gate* (widen it from operator margin to any interested principal, and from authorization to presentation). Residual row 23 upgrades, anti-shadow criterion 9 gets a real reconciliation path, and my own proposed kill condition 7 substantially weakens.

**Where I pushed back on Knox, and why it matters.** Knox said my "Palantir works inside one enrollment" was stale and that Palantir now federates ontologies across enrollments — which would have knocked out a moat claim the estate has been carrying. I verified it. My wording *was* stale and is withdrawn: Peer Manager genuinely peers object data across two enrollments with directional, marking-controlled connections. But Palantir's own developer community answers the link-type question flatly — *"At the moment, no there is no way to do this… tracking as a feature request"* — and the documented workaround is duplicating the object into each ontology. **Data peers; the ontology does not.** More decisively, peering presupposes both sides running Foundry and jointly configuring the connection. Our problem is asymmetric, non-consenting, non-co-platformed principals. A payer, a pharmacy, a lender and a patient will never be co-enrolled in one vendor's platform by mutual agreement. So the moat survives — on a corrected basis, which is worth more than the stale one.

The second pushback: Knox's "cross-plane conformance contract" is the right architectural move and the wrong provenance. It's presented as a new category, but C4.6's `C1`–`C16` **already is** a conformance layer that owns no truth and which every downstream build must pass. So I mapped the profile's obligations onto the landed pattern instead of minting Knox's category. Seven of the ten anti-shadow criteria fall onto existing C4.6 gates, an eighth onto the Accountability threshold law, and only two small financing-specific gates are owed. That dissolves R0's dead end — where I'd concluded three criteria simply couldn't be demonstrated — without creating a governance god-object.

**The piece that's mine, and it's the one you'll care about.** Your nuclear-command instinct, relayed through Knox, exposed something both of us had missed: authority decomposes into **three** things, not two. Fact authority (who may assert this fact — C3.6C). Action authority (who may commit this action, in this capacity, now). And **execution admissibility** — may this proceed at all, given conditions that are not about authority. *A valid order is not an executable order.* A payer authorization does not create clinical appropriateness; a clinical order does not create inventory; inventory does not create consent; a valid prescription does not create pharmacy acceptance.

That unifies with the aviation finding into one mechanism I've named **conjunctive admission**: an execution proceeds only when every non-fungible predicate holds, any predicate-holder may withhold, and withholding is not a contest of authority — it's the absence of a condition, so no holder acquires anyone else's authority. Clinician holds indication. Patient holds consent. Pharmacist holds professional acceptance. Payer holds funding — and its withholding produces *not funded*, never *not indicated*. Supply holds availability. D6 holds money state.

That is the physics of care stated in one line, and it is precisely why no single incumbent can legitimately own this end to end: each of them holds exactly one predicate. It's also why Axis 2 has to exist — something must compose the predicates without owning any of them. I attached the transfer limit in the same breath, because the dangerous misreading is using dual-concurrence to hand a payer a co-equal vote on a clinical act, which would invert Law 2 while looking like rigor.

I also inverted Knox's strategic answer to the non-participating payer. Unilateral coherence → bilateral upgrade is right, and I adopted it. But Knox doesn't name its cost: **unilateral mode is exactly where the profile is most tempted to become a shadow source of truth**, because when we reconstruct payer positions from documents and portals with no payer in the loop, our derived assessment is the only coherent artifact in the room. The strategy that answers kill condition 6 *raises* kill condition 5. Three conditions make it survivable and they're now stated wherever the strategy is.

**On my own work:** a first draft of R1 stated Knox's corrected tally as R1's own and failed to propagate a row upgrade I'd just made — the identical defect class I was fixing. I caught it by recounting mechanically rather than re-reading. All three tallies are now shown separately. R0's "six of eight gap rows are generic physics" was wrong on numerator *and* denominator and flattered the result; corrected to four of nine, each backed by the estate's own words. And Knox was right that "never build payer adjudication" contradicted my own trace 7, where an OMNI federation is the risk-bearing principal — that's now *never impersonate another principal's determination*, with a four-dimension sourcing matrix replacing the single column.

**On durable homes.** You told me to get these into their right spots and not bolt them on. The constraint is real: `PRESPINE-PHASEA-INTEGRATOR` is vacant and shared control-plane surfaces are read-only to me. So §17 is a **verbatim-ready landing packet** — the exact appended text for the existing comparator registry Palantir row, exact dispositions for `D0INS-REV-002` and `REV-185`, two new open-review rows, the `9p` route extension, the catalog row. Mechanically landable, no re-derivation. The Palantir correction goes into the *existing* registry row, not another Palantir essay — Knox is right that the registry exists to stop that cycle. The `C6` breadth extension and the C4.6 §11 loyalty-guard enumeration gap are raised **to C4.6's own gate**, not written into accepted L2 doctrine. Execution admissibility and conjunctive admission route to C3.6C/A-Q16, RBAC, CNS and Care as generic authority physics — they are explicitly *not* Insurance's to own.

Verdict holds at **`SURVIVES_WITH_NAMED_RECONCILIATIONS`** — same name, different basis: lower confidence on discharge, higher on repairability. R0's "14/14 produced, 6/6 performed" is withdrawn as a completeness claim, replaced by an explicit discharge posture. Eight named reconciliations, none of them Insurance-owned.

But three load-bearing claims are still wrong or overclaimed:

First: the three explicit questions Opus asked
1. Does the C6 extension scope hold?

Yes as a reusable proof family. No as currently described.

Opus’s discovery is real and important. C4.6 already contains:

C6 | Neutrality / incentive firewall | margin-only counterfactual test | FAILS if changing operator margin changes clinical authorization, or hides incentive lineage in selection.

That means Insurance should extend an existing proof pattern, not invent the idea from scratch. It also confirms that the pharmacy arc had already found the same underlying economic-influence physics.

But R1 overstates what this buys:

C4.6 is accepted analysis-nonbinding L2 doctrine and a conformance instrument.
C6 is a test specification with a named failure condition.
It is not proof that an input-visibility boundary, audit instrumentation, test harness, or runtime enforcement has been built.
It does not identify the canonical owner of the cross-cutting economics law.
REV-185 is a review row, not an architectural owner.

Therefore residual row 23 should not upgrade from NAMED-GAP to OWNED-DELTA merely because a proof shape exists. The honest disposition is closer to:

NAMED-GAP_WITH_EXISTING_CONFORMANCE_PATTERN

Using the existing allowed vocabulary, keep it NAMED-GAP and record C6 as the strongest existing proof mechanism. Consequently, R1’s actual residual tally should remain 1 OWNED / 9 OWNED-DELTA / 10 NAMED-GAP / 3 EXTERNAL until the enforcement owner and runtime boundary are settled.

The generalized Insurance test needs four distinct probes:

Probe	What changes	What must remain invariant
Clinical-merit invariance	payer/PBM/manufacturer/lender/operator/OMNI economics	clinical indication, clinical acceptability, contraindication, clinical rationale
Feasible-set legibility	funding, price, deductible, availability	original clinical option remains visible and separately attributed even if presently infeasible
Presentation integrity	interested-principal economics	economic preference must not be rendered as clinical priority or equivalence
Selection integrity	objective, incentive, authorized selector	incentive lineage remains inspectable; patient preference and affordability remain legitimate inputs

The important subtlety: some outputs should change when affordability or a funding condition changes. What may not change is the statement of clinical merit. That is the exact Law‑2/Law‑3 boundary.

Also, the result repeatedly points to “C4.6 §7” for C1–C16. The conformance table is in C4.6 §12, not §7. That pointer needs correction.

2. Does “conjunctive admission” survive the transfer-limit test?

It survives as one admission topology. It does not survive as the universal architecture law R1 currently makes it.

The aviation case is genuinely conjunctive: the PIC and dispatcher must both believe the flight can safely proceed before release, and either can stop the release on safety grounds. That is a real, useful high-reliability mechanism.

But care execution is not always one giant AND expression. It can involve:

conjunction;
alternative authorized actors;
threshold conditions;
precedence;
sequencing;
temporary unavailability;
explicit waiver;
default on silence;
emergency or break-glass transition;
legally nonwaivable prohibition;
patient refusal;
professional refusal;
funding that affects feasibility but not clinical validity.

So the durable model should be a typed execution-admission policy, with “conjunctive admission” retained as one special pattern—like joint release—not the whole constitution.

A useful noncanonical working shape is:

required positive commits
hard prohibitions
resource/capability availability
evidence/knowledge sufficiency
patient choice or refusal
funding conditions
default-on-silence behavior
waiver / exception authority
break-glass authority
transfer / successor-acceptance condition
responsibility continuity

Each condition then has semantics such as:

must_be_true
must_not_be_true
must_be_committed_by
must_be_available_from
may_be_unknown_with_fallback
waivable_by
break_glass_by
default_on_silence
blocks_create
blocks_fund
blocks_execute
blocks_fulfill
warns_but_does_not_block

This is not a new domain or truth object. It is the typed composition needed to prevent unlike conditions from being flattened.

One serious defect in R1’s current predicate table

R1 includes payer funding and D6 money state among the predicates whose withholding prevents execution.

That cannot be universal. OMNI’s accepted care-financing physics explicitly preserve:

care with no financing lifecycle;
uncompensated care;
emergency care;
care before settlement;
payment state ≠ care state;
financing affects feasibility without authoring indication.

The Gate‑1a physics says care does not logically entail a financing lifecycle, and financing is insufficient to create provider capacity, consent, clinical authority, resources, or fulfillment.

A payer may withhold funding. D6 may report not settled. Neither universally means execution inadmissible.

Your nuclear-launch challenge: the actual architecture it exposes

You are right not to accept that one analogy automatically generated the right rule.

The different nuclear scenarios are not variants of a single authority question. They are exposing several orthogonal dimensions:

Scenario	What it actually tests
Provider wants to act and should act	clinical judgment + action authority + admissibility
Provider refuses, another person acts	actual committer · represented principal · delegation/coverage · accepted transfer · unauthorized action
Pharmacy removed the option because it is dangerous	professional or institutional prohibition · policy authority · clinical disagreement
Pharmacy allows it but has none in stock	temporary resource/capability unavailability, not a change in clinical meaning
Provider does not know an attack occurred	exposure/knowledge sufficiency · source latency · decision-context freshness · duty to notify
Provider wants to act; OMNI disagrees	what kind of disagreement is OMNI expressing: model suggestion, uncertainty warning, deterministic safety rule, legal prohibition, operator policy, or economic preference?
Someone acts and harm follows	professional duty · care ownership · execution custody · legal-entity exposure · actual committer · influence lineage · later legal adjudication

The durable distinction should therefore be at least:

Fact or epistemic authority — who may assert, adopt, correct, or supersede a fact?
Decision or action authority — who may commit this action in this represented capacity?
Execution admissibility — may it proceed now under the applicable safety, legal, consent, resource, and professional constraints?
Capability and availability — can the executor actually perform it?
Responsibility continuity — who retains care duty, custody, or follow-through until a successor actually accepts?
Liability evidence — what facts must be preserved for later professional, contractual, insurer, regulator, or court adjudication?

R1 currently stops after the first three and treats the third too conjunctively.

The OMNI-disagrees case must be typed

“OMNI disagrees” cannot be one thing.

OMNI output	Authority consequence
Model recommendation or prediction	advisory candidate; no veto
Missing/stale/degraded context warning	may require review, consult, or narrower action; does not author the clinical conclusion
Deterministic consent or legal prohibition	hard gate if the governing policy and jurisdiction actually authorize it
Ratified safety floor	may block or require break-glass under its explicit authority
Operator preference	no clinical authority
Payer/funder preference	funding consequence only
Economic optimization	cannot masquerade as clinical merit
Runtime malfunction	degrade automation and escalate; never fabricate certainty

That is the serious version of your example.

Legal responsibility must not be “solved” by architecture

The repository has already reasoned about this.

The multi-principal run explicitly concluded:

audit is provenance, not verdict;
competence and liability are later governed adjudications;
preserve factual responsibility and influence lineage;
distinguish who committed, under what authority, what was shown, accepted, rejected, checked, and what happened later;
transfer of care is different from consultation or operational delegation.

The successor adversarial run explicitly rejected the proposition that architecture allocates legal liability, while requiring the system to distinguish professional/legal duty, commit authority, custody, coordination, visibility, and proof.

So the durable rule is not:

“The provider is liable,” or “OMNI is liable.”

It is:

OMNI must preserve enough principal, capacity, authority, commitment, custody, transfer, influence, evidence, policy-version, and outcome lineage that the rightful legal and professional process can determine responsibility without the architecture having pre-decided it.

That prior depth should be explicitly inherited by R2.

{"path":"/workspace/.cursor/plans/v4_INS_G2_operating_composition_and_sufficiency_result_2026-08-09.md","streamContent":"## §20 — Is Insurance a cousin? — the cross-cutting finding, and where it belongs (R2)\n\n**This section exists because the operator asked a question the arc could not answer from inside itself, and the estate had already answered it twice without either arc noticing.**\n\n### §20.1 The answer: yes, and the estate said so twice\n**C4.6 §0.5** answers the identical question form for pharmacy, verbatim: *\"is pharmacy just another version of fulfillment? is it distinct? a cousin of ordinary vendor supply?\"* — **\"the answer is cousin: shared substrate, specialized profile — neither a silo nor a twin.\"** Its stack: GCE (shared, ratified) → counterparty participation/capability profiles → distinct native lifecycles → adapter family + connection instance → projection owning no truth. Its ruling: *\"Pharmacy is NOT a new OMNI-owned unified lifecycle or truth-owning domain… OMNI composes a profile over the shared exchange and does not absorb it.\"*\n\n**Gate-1b's Axis 2 reached the same shape independently:** a **first-class composed operating profile** over source-native owners and generic GCE, owning no source truth. **Two arcs, no contact, identical verdict.**\n\n> **Insurance is a cousin of Pharmacy, and both are cousins of labs/diagnostics, vendor supply and any future external-counterparty loop. The shared substrate is GCE + native lifecycles + adapter/connection + projection. What differs is only the specialized profile: pharmacy's is prescriber authority, prescription lineage, pharmacist review and refusal, substitution envelope, licensure and controlled-substance regime; Insurance's is coverage relationship identity, funding conditions, benefit interpretation, determination and appeal, financing arrangement and patient responsibility.**\n\n**This raises confidence in Axis 2 rather than threatening it.** Convergence of two independent arcs on one shape is evidence the shape is physics rather than an Insurance-specific accommodation. **It also correctly shrinks Gate 2's job:** not *invent a mixed-financing architecture*, but *inherit the shared substrate and specify only the financing profile.* Most of §1's four strata are the cousin substrate, not Insurance's invention — which is why §5's row drive found no new truth-owning object. **It is not a reroute of the arc; it is the arc's own result, recognised.**\n\n### §20.2 Why the underlying physics is worth finding at all — the operator's existential question, answered without mysticism\n*Doesn't Palantir just ingest everything and link it up? Isn't that the pattern?*\n\n**That is genuinely the pattern for legibility, and it is not the pattern for law.** An ontology makes a domain *representable and operable*. It does not tell you that a payer's equivalence claim may never reach clinical adoption, that a stock-out is a readiness state and not an inadmissibility, or that a coverage denial must not erase a recommendation. **Those are not derivable from the data model — they are invariants that must be supplied.** Care §19's ratified `[INV]` is exactly this: a generic ontology can *configure toward* the composition and cannot *supply* it.\n\nSo the physics buys three specific things, and they are the 1BN/10BN argument stated plainly:\n1. **Loop N gets cheap.** If Insurance is a cousin, the fifth and fortieth external loop inherit the substrate and specify only a profile. **That is the compounding**, and it is why \"is this a cousin?\" is a commercial question, not a taxonomic one.\n2. **Loop N gets safe.** A violation of a cross-loop invariant is *invisible in the schema* and *catastrophic in care*. Physics is what makes the violation detectable at build time — which is precisely what a conformance gate like `C6` or `C12` is for.\n3. **The substrate survives substitution.** Models, rails, vendors and even ontologies change. What must remain true across all of them is the constitution. **That is the moat sentence the estate already ratified, and it is the one claim that does not depend on any incumbent's current capability.**\n\n### §20.3 Where this gets recorded so it stops evaporating — the mechanism already exists and is under-scoped\nThe operator's sharpest question is *where does a builder record that these are linked patterns, so we stop ping-ponging.* **The machine exists: Care §19's Homology Matrix, with the verdict vocabulary `SHARED-LAW · ANALOGOUS · CARE-SPECIFIC · OPEN`, plus §1b's law-scope crosswalk that propagates `U` laws, refuses to propagate `C` laws, and keeps `A` analogous.**\n\n**Its defect is scope, in two ways, and both are small to fix:**\n- **It has three columns — Care, Platform, Accountability.** Pharmacy (C4.6) and Insurance were both built afterwards and **neither was added**. Every shared law each of them needed was therefore re-derived. `C6` is the proof: pharmacy independently re-derived the recommendation-integrity firewall that Care already carries as a `U` law.\n- **It lives inside one loop's capture**, so it is found only by someone already reading Care — the identical discovery failure the Comparator Registry was created to fix for comparators, and the identical failure `D0CKPT-GRD-004` names for boot surfaces.\n\n**Proposed, not minted, and deliberately using only existing machinery:**\n\n> **The Homology Obligation.** A new loop, profile or cousin arc **cannot close** until it has (a) added its column to the homology matrix, (b) declared per dimension `SHARED-LAW | ANALOGOUS | SPECIFIC | OPEN`, and (c) declared its `U/C/A` law-scope inheritance. Enforcement is Gate-1b §15.1 **part E** — a named consuming gate that cannot pass without disposing of the finding — applied to *inheritance* rather than to *output*.\n\nNothing new is invented: the matrix exists (Care §19), the vocabulary exists (§19 + §1b `U/C/A`), and the enforcement pattern exists (§15.1 part E). **The matrix's home is the open question** — it is cross-cutting and currently lives in Care. Candidate homes: promote to the doctrine spine beside the Comparator Registry, or hold it as a Reactor-class registry. **Not decided here — this is an Insurance gate and the matrix is not Insurance's to move.** Routed at §17.\n\n**Insurance's own column is owed and is NOT authored here.** Doing it properly requires the two carriers §0.7 records as unconsumed (C3.8 G4; `EVRUN-000007 §02` / `EVRUN-000008`). **Authoring a column from an arc that has not read its inputs is how this problem started.**\n\n### §20.4 What this does not license\nNo new domain, no new object, no new registry minted, no Insurance ownership of Care's admissibility model, no reopening of C4.6, and no change to the Gate-2 verdict. **§20 changes what Gate 2 claims to have discovered, not what Gate 2 concluded.**\n\n---\n\n## §19 — STOP RECEIPT"}

Nick — you were right, and I verified it rather than taking your word or Knox's. Here's what I found.

**Care §5b already contains the entire thing.** Its heading is *"Care-transition admissibility (the '10 things must align' physics; per-action-type, NOT one god-gate)."* Four projections, each mapped to an existing owner — decision admissibility, execution authorization, execution readiness, consequence-and-proof contract — with an explicit `[INV]`: *"Do NOT collapse to one boolean; these compile into one transition VIEW but never one admissibility TRUTH-object."*

Your nuclear scenarios aren't adjacent to it. They **are** it, one by one:

| What you asked | Care §5b state, already written |
|---|---|
| pharmacy pulled it from formulary because it's dangerous | prohibition under projection 1 |
| pharmacy would allow it, just out of stock | **`indicated+accepted-but-operationally-unavailable` — readiness, NOT inadmissibility** |
| provider doesn't know Korea launched 5 minutes ago | **`unresolved-because-evidence-stale`** + *action-critical freshness* |
| provider refuses, someone else acts | projection 2 — role/scope/delegation, plus §9a *contributions ≠ votes* |
| coverage denies it | **`appropriate-but-not-covered` — commercial, not clinical** |
| provider's right, OMNI disagrees | §5b.1's automation axes, with `[INV]` **AI is not a Care-validity condition** |

The exact distinction you drew — *taken out because dangerous* versus *just offline, will restock* — is the difference between prohibition and readiness, and Care wrote it as a named state. And yes, to your side question: Care does cover sequencing. §5b.1's `checkpoint_graph` is versioned ordered nodes with timing, preconditions, blocking semantics, fallback, reauthorization triggers and timeout/escalation. Knox's ad-hoc list of waiver, break-glass, default-on-silence and non-waivable prohibition is Care's `authority_basis` enum, which includes `emergency_authority` and `court/statutory_authority`. Care's own header even says the earlier versions of those enums *"were malformed"* — meaning this was already litigated once and corrected.

So I withdrew O-2 as new and demoted O-3. "Conjunctive admission" is `dual_control` — **one value in an existing six-value enum**. I built a general law out of one enum value and dressed it in a federal aviation regulation. Care's decomposition is better than mine, because separating readiness from consequence is what makes an unavailable option a *reroute* instead of a *denial* — and I collapsed exactly those two.

**The cause is mechanical, not mystical.** Route `9p` — the Gate-2 read floor — routes the Insurance chain and nothing else. Gate-1b's own estate matrix cites the Care capture lines for precisely these facts, so Gate 1b *had* them, and the route carried none forward. A gate that inherits only its own arc will re-derive every cross-cutting law it needs and believe each re-derivation is a discovery. That's `GRD-043` operating on inheritance instead of output. Nothing evaporated — it was never routed in.

**Your cousin question: yes, and the estate answered it twice.** C4.6 §0.5 asks your question in your words — *"is pharmacy just another version of fulfillment? is it distinct? a cousin of ordinary vendor supply?"* — and answers **"cousin: shared substrate, specialized profile — neither a silo nor a twin."** Gate-1b's Axis 2 independently landed on the same shape for Insurance. Two arcs, no contact, identical verdict. Shared substrate is GCE plus native lifecycles plus adapter/connection plus projection; what differs is only the profile — pharmacy's is prescriber authority and prescription lineage and pharmacist refusal, Insurance's is coverage identity and funding conditions and determination/appeal. You weren't leading me astray. That convergence is *evidence Axis 2 is real*, and it shrinks Gate 2's job rather than expanding it.

**Where it gets recorded — the machine exists and nobody scoped it.** Care §19 is a **Homology Matrix** with a fixed verdict vocabulary (`SHARED-LAW · ANALOGOUS · CARE-SPECIFIC · OPEN`), plus §1b's `U/C/A` law-scope crosswalk that propagates universal laws to other loops and refuses to propagate care-specific ones. That is exactly the "how does a builder record linked patterns" mechanism you were reaching for. **It has three columns — Care, Platform, Accountability — and we've since built at least two more loops that were never added.** So Pharmacy re-derived the economic firewall as `C6`; Insurance re-derived admissibility. And it lives *inside the Care capture*, so only someone reading Care ever finds it — the same discovery failure the Comparator Registry was built to cure for comparators and `D0CKPT-GRD-004` names for boot surfaces.

I proposed one thing, minting nothing: **the Homology Obligation** — a new loop, profile or cousin arc cannot close until it adds its column, declares per-dimension `SHARED-LAW | ANALOGOUS | SPECIFIC | OPEN`, and declares its `U/C/A` inheritance. Enforcement is the "named consuming gate" pattern Gate-1b already invented. Matrix, vocabulary and enforcement all exist. Where the matrix should *live* is an open question and it is not Insurance's to move, so I routed it rather than deciding it.

**On Palantir: it was the wrong fight, and I'm ending it rather than winning it.** Knox and I have now flip-flopped twice on whether link types peer across enrollments. I checked the canonical Peer Manager page and it lists objects, object sets and Gotham files; Knox is reading a different surface. Both readings and their sources are recorded, the question is marked `OPEN`, my proposed registry append is **withdrawn with no replacement**, and it goes to the Evidence Plane and the C3.8 arc's owner. Because Care §19 already carries the ratified answer, and it's better than all three of our drafts: *a generic ontology can **configure toward** the composition but cannot **supply** it.* Whether Palantir crosses an enrollment boundary is a capability question. Whether an ontology can supply enforced non-fungible authority and clinical adoption is a category question. We spent the arc on the wrong axis.

**That's also your existential question answered without magic.** Why chase the physics? Three things, concretely. I agree with your instinct about the importance of this relay. I do not agree that R2 has yet discovered and connected “the core of OMNI” cleanly enough to accept it.

What R2 has uncovered is more precise:

OMNI needs an explicit mechanism for identifying recurring architectural patterns, separating their shared laws from their permitted variations, and forcing each new loop/profile to declare what it inherits, specializes, rejects, and still leaves open.

That is foundational. It is also not yet the same thing as the current Care Homology Matrix, and it is not automatically solved by adding Pharmacy and Insurance as two more columns.

It correctly found that R1’s supposedly new execution-admissibility model was already present—more richly decomposed—in the Care capture, and that dual_control was only one approval topology rather than a universal law. It also correctly recognized that narrow arc-only routing causes cross-cutting laws to be rediscovered as if they were new.

But R2 overstates both the maturity and the scope of what it found.

First correction: Care did not “already settle” this

The Care capture is:

analysis_nonbinding;
REVIEW-DRAFT;
explicitly not closed;
and its own reading key defines [INV] as a candidate invariant—proposed, not ratified.

Its source-adjudication section says the admissibility composition is a COMPOSES_EXISTING synthesis of scattered prior pieces, not a newly ratified constitutional object. It also records real conflicts and open reconciliation.

So the accurate statement is not:

“Care §5b already contains the settled answer.”

It is:

Care §5b contains the strongest current candidate decomposition, assembled from existing authoritative pieces, but the cross-loop composition itself remains review-draft.

That distinction matters. Otherwise we have merely replaced ad hoc reinvention with status laundering.

The same applies to the Homology Matrix. It exists. It is valuable. It is not yet a governing cross-loop control plane.

R2 also still has a mechanical propagation defect: the current file begins with GATE-2 RESULT (R1) and declares artifact status R1, while its state table says R2.

That is small architecturally, but it is an almost comic demonstration of the exact propagation problem under discussion.

Second correction: this was not independent convergence

R2 says:

“Two arcs, no contact, identical verdict.”

But the same R2 says Gate‑1b’s estate matrix cited the Care capture and therefore “had” these facts.

Those cannot both be true in the strong sense.

What we have is:

cross-arc recurrence under incomplete propagation

That is still meaningful. Pharmacy and Insurance repeatedly exhibit the same architectural shape. But it is not blind independent convergence evidence, because the Insurance arc had at least some Care and Pharmacy inheritance available.

The finding is therefore slightly weaker scientifically but more important operationally:

The estate can locate the right pattern and still fail to make that pattern usable by the next builder.

That is the real defect.

Third correction: not every external loop is one cousin family

R2 currently says Insurance and Pharmacy are cousins of labs/diagnostics, vendor supply, and “any future external-counterparty loop.”

That is too broad.

They are certainly related, but cousinhood is altitude- and dimension-specific.

A lab can simultaneously be:

an external counterparty;
an evidence producer;
an order fulfiller;
a professional interpreter;
a regulated facility;
and a source whose result may or may not be clinically adopted.

A lender is an external counterparty and commitment issuer, but it is not an evidence-to-clinical-adoption loop.

A pharmacy is an external counterparty, a professional execution authority, a sourcing candidate, a fulfiller, and sometimes a clinical-change participant.

Therefore one loop may instantiate multiple recurring archetypes. A single table with one column per “loop” will flatten this.

The likely OMNI archetype families

These are candidates, not accepted taxonomy:

Archetype family	Examples	Shared core	Specialized variation
Evidence → attributed meaning	intake, documents, labs, imaging, wearables, outside records	raw evidence · source identity · extraction/normalization · verification · adoption/rejection · correction lineage	units/reference ranges · imaging interpretation · document attestation · patient-report rules
External-principal participation	payer, pharmacy, lender, sponsor, lab/facility, supplier, public program	principal/capacity · GCE crossing · relationship/connection · assertion/commitment/custody typing · source-preserving projection	funding determination · professional acceptance · credit approval · sponsorship · statutory authority
Order → acceptance → fulfillment	appointment, procedure, prescription, lab draw, referral, shipment	request/order · acceptance · resource reservation · execution · evidence · exception · reopen	clinical scope · inventory · controlled-substance law · venue/resource semantics
Governed resolution / selection	care recommit, sourcing, benefit interpretation, appeal, identity conflict, correction impact	candidates/positions · authority · disagreement · operative posture · commit · reconsider/reopen	clinical adoption · economic allocation · source precedence · legal mandate
Obligation / custody / continuity	care follow-up, appeal deadline, remedy, notice, regulatory duty, response case	accepted duty · owner · clock · transfer/successor acceptance · no-orphan rule · closure	clinical responsibility · contractual remedy · statutory deadline · communication obligation
Projection / human operating context	patient view, provider workspace, ops queue, owner analytics, portable profile	source references · derivation/version · audience policy · validity/invalidation · no independent authority	persona-specific explanation, metrics, controls, privacy
Versioned definition / policy	clinical pathways, payer policies, catalog, consent forms, sourcing rules, pricing definitions	version · effective period · precedence · applicability · supersession	clinical, contractual, economic, jurisdictional semantics

These groups overlap. That is not a bug. It means the right control structure cannot be “every artifact belongs to one loop family.”

What is not a cousin group

Some things are constitutional axes across every family:

authority;
consent;
time and partial ordering;
provenance;
correction;
uncertainty;
portability;
economic-influence separation;
proof;
legal/responsibility lineage.

These are not another loop family. They are dimensions every profile must pass through.

Likewise:

Clinical Memory and D6 are not lifecycle cousins merely because both version records.
Surfaces are not truth-owning loop cousins.
Rails and adapters are not domains.
Participants and principals are not loop types.
Two things being visible in one patient journey does not make them homologous.

That discipline is what prevents “everything is a cousin” from becoming the next god-model.

The real established concept is not “Homology Obligation”

You are correct that we are not the first people to confront this.

The closest established disciplines are:

1. Software product-line engineering

Software product-line engineering builds a portfolio from a core asset base, while explicitly modeling planned variability so product-specific adaptations do not repeatedly reinvent or damage the common core. The SEI’s language is almost exactly the problem OMNI now faces: unmanaged variability causes duplicate mechanisms, incompatible variation choices, and missed required variations.

2. Reference architecture + profiles

FHIR has a base specification plus profiles and Implementation Guides that restrict and extend the base for particular domains, countries, institutions, vendors, and workflows. Its profiling model explicitly allows overlapping adaptations, and its conformance resources make the inherited and specialized rules computable.

This is particularly relevant because a FHIR resource can participate in multiple profile hierarchies—exactly the multi-membership problem above.

3. Integration profiles

IHE profiles define recurring combinations of actors, transactions, required groupings, and options. A product can implement multiple actors and multiple profiles, and claiming conformance requires supporting each profile’s required transactions rather than merely sharing a data model.

4. Core framework + workload lenses

AWS applies the core Well-Architected Framework and then allows multiple official or custom lenses to add workload-specific questions, best practices, and improvement plans. One workload can carry multiple lenses.

These are not exact OMNI templates, but together they point to the right concept:

A profiled reference architecture with explicit commonality, variability, and conformance.

That is the real industry-grade description.

“Homology Matrix” is a useful analytic tool.
“Homology Obligation” is a useful temporary phrase.
Neither is yet the best build-facing name.

What OMNI actually needs

The elegant control structure is not one ever-widening matrix. It is a two-level pattern/profile system.

Level 1 — Cross-loop archetype registry

Each archetype records:

archetype_id
purpose and scope
source lineage and maturity
shared invariants
shared lifecycle/interaction shape
forbidden collapses
variation points
required conformance tests
known counterexamples
current member profiles

Examples might eventually include:

evidence_to_attributed_meaning
external_principal_participation
governed_resolution
ordered_fulfillment
obligation_continuity
versioned_projection

Those names are illustrative, not proposed canon.

Level 2 — Per-loop/profile declaration

Insurance, Pharmacy, Labs, Referrals, or a future lender profile declares:

instantiates:
  - external_principal_participation
  - governed_resolution
  - obligation_continuity

inherits:
  - source authority
  - proposal ≠ commit
  - correction never rewrites history
  - projection ≠ authority

specializes:
  - funding_condition
  - benefit-policy version
  - appeal / recoupment
  - patient responsibility

does_not_inherit:
  - clinical adoption authority
  - pharmacist substitution authority

native_truth_owners:
  ...

required_conformance_gates:
  ...

open_variances:
  ...

A loop may instantiate several archetypes. That is what a simple column matrix cannot express well.

Closure obligation

A new loop/profile cannot close until it states:

which archetypes it instantiates;
which shared laws it inherits;
what it specializes;
what it explicitly does not inherit;
which truth owners and correction laws remain native;
which conformance tests prove the composition;
which deviations remain open.

That is the durable version of Opus’s “Homology Obligation.”

I would call the candidate mechanism:

Pattern Inheritance and Variance Declaration

or, more product-line-like:

Archetype/Profile Conformance Declaration

The final name should wait until the existing Care, Platform, Accountability, Pharmacy, Insurance, C3.8, and Reactor materials are reconciled.

Where this belongs

Not inside Insurance.

Not inside Care.

Not inside the Comparator Registry.

Not inside OMNI Reactor.

The likely home is the architecture-memory control plane:

the System Map or architecture canon indexes the archetypes;
rich pattern contracts live in dedicated pattern/profile artifacts;
the read graph routes every new loop to relevant archetypes;
the build-entry gate requires a profile declaration;
conformance fixtures prove inheritance;
the open-review and decision ledgers record unresolved variance and promotion state.

The Comparator Registry answers:

“What external systems or industries illuminate OMNI?”

This new mechanism answers:

“Which internal OMNI architecture patterns recur, and exactly how does this profile inherit or vary them?”

OMNI Reactor is also not the owner of this. Reactor may turn out to be one major archetype or constitutional pattern—intent-to-consequence continuity—but making it the registry would objectify it into the universal god-layer its own capture warns against. The prior multi-principal and adversarial work also explicitly distinguishes factual responsibility, influence lineage, custody, authority, and later legal adjudication rather than allowing architecture to pre-assign liability.

What Palantir can and cannot do

R2’s formulation—

“An ontology supplies legibility; it cannot supply the law.”

—is close, but still too absolute.

A Palantir-class platform can:

represent the law;
encode it in types, relationships, actions, permissions, and functions;
enforce it once authored;
trace decisions and writes;
distribute the operational representation.

What it does not do merely by ingesting and linking data is:

derive which distinctions are normatively required;
establish their clinical or legal legitimacy;
decide which principal has rightful authority;
determine which correction law is morally or professionally valid;
guarantee that the representation remains portable and non-captive;
own the healthcare constitution.

The sharper line is:

A generic ontology can express and enforce an authored constitution. It does not originate, legitimate, or own that constitution.

That is not mystical. It is the difference between:

an expressive execution platform; and
the domain laws the platform must implement.

The C3.8 terminus already moved OMNI toward the right posture: a composed semantic/ontology layer over domain-owned truth, contracts, source authority, and projections—not a new domain, god-object, or proprietary lock-in.

The current Palantir product-capability dispute should still be resolved in the Evidence Plane because factual accuracy matters. But OMNI’s moat must not depend on Palantir lacking a specific current feature.

Why finding the physics matters

It matters only when it produces engineering and operating leverage.

A candidate “physics” law earns elevation when it:

recurs across materially different contexts;
preserves the same authority and correction behavior;
survives counterexamples;
names the owners of its parts;
produces a falsifiable conformance test;
reduces later build work;
and does not force unlike truths into one lifecycle.

The practical benefits are:

Build leverage

The fortieth profile should not rebuild identity, authority, exchange, custody, projection, correction, and proof.

Safety

A payer preference becoming clinical adoption is not a schema defect. It is a constitutional defect. A pattern registry plus conformance tests can detect it.

Adaptability

Rails, vendors, models, and user interfaces change. Pattern-level law lets OMNI swap implementations without re-deciding the meaning of care.

Product coherence

Shared laws produce a coherent patient/provider/operator experience across different loops without forcing one universal backend object.

Strategic moat

OMNI’s moat is not merely having more linked data. It is the governed, reusable, testable composition of healthcare-specific authority, consent, responsibility, continuity, economics, correction, and proof.

What infinite compute should do

Do not send one hundred agents down one hundred lanes and hope convergence appears.

The right operating cycle is:

1. Mine existing arcs for recurring candidate patterns.
2. Cluster them without promoting them.
3. Pressure them against counterexamples and non-cousins.
4. Ratify the smallest shared core.
5. Publish the archetype and its conformance tests.
6. Require every later profile to declare inheritance and variance.
7. Use agents to test, compare, and detect drift—not to independently reinvent the core.

This is bottom-up discovery followed by top-down propagation.

Infinite compute should buy:

broader counterexample generation;
faster corpus comparison;
exhaustive variance analysis;
automated conformance;
stale-reference detection.

It should not buy infinite duplicate doctrine.

Remove “two arcs, no contact.” Replace with cross-arc recurrence under incomplete propagation.

Hold the name “Homology Obligation.” Reframe it as a candidate archetype/profile declaration mechanism.
Do not enlarge the Care matrix by columns yet. First extract candidate archetypes from Care, Platform, Accountability, Pharmacy, Insurance, C3.8, and Reactor.
Consume the named inheritance debt—C3.8 G4 and EVRUN‑000007/000008—before authoring the Insurance profile declaration.
Separate pattern authority from profile conformance. A shared pattern must have maturity, sources, owners, and tests; a profile declares its usage.

Keep Insurance responsible for proving its composition, even when the source law belongs elsewhere.
No C3.9, no E2, no integrator landing.
